title: Quadratic Equation Word Problems
seo_title: Sec 3 Quadratic word problems Worksheets: Free Secondary 3 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: formulating a quadratic equation in one variable to solve problems
meta_desc: Free Secondary 3 maths worksheets on quadratic equation word problems: forming the equation, number problems, rectangles, paths, right-angled triangles, heights and answers to 2 decimal places. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Form the equation, make one side 0, solve, then check each root makes sense.
key_sub: Reject negative lengths and times, and answer the exact question asked.
body_html:
How it works

  1. Let the unknown be x and write the other quantities in terms of x.
  2. Form an equation, expand and make one side 0.
  3. Solve by factorising, or by the formula if it does not factorise.
  4. Check each root in the problem. Reject a negative length, time or number of people, then answer the question asked.
Example

A rectangle is 3 cm longer than it is wide. Its area is 40 cm². Find its length.

x(x + 3) = 40, so x² + 3x − 40 = 0

(x − 5)(x + 8) = 0, so x = 5 (reject −8)

Answer: 8 cm

Example

The sides of a right-angled triangle are x, x + 7 and x + 8 cm. Find x.

x² + (x + 7)² = (x + 8)²

x² − 2x − 15 = 0, so (x − 5)(x + 3) = 0

Answer: x = 5

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to make one side 0 before factorising.
  • Keeping the negative root when the answer is a length or a time.
  • Giving x when the question asks for the length, which may be x + 3.
  • Squaring only part of a bracket: (x + 7)² = x² + 14x + 49, not x² + 49.

faq.q: How do I form a quadratic equation from a word problem?
faq.a: Choose x for one unknown, write the others in terms of x, and use the fact given (area, product, Pythagoras' theorem or a formula) to write an equation. Then make one side 0.

faq.q: What do I do with the negative root?
faq.a: Check it in the problem. A length, time, speed or number of objects cannot be negative, so reject it and say why.

faq.q: When should I use the formula instead of factorising?
faq.a: When the quadratic does not factorise, or when the question asks for answers correct to 2 decimal places or 3 significant figures.

faq.q: Why does a thrown ball reach the same height twice?
faq.a: It passes that height once going up and once coming down, so the quadratic has two positive roots.

items.q: A rectangle is (x + 7) cm long and x cm wide. Its area is 24 cm². Which equation is correct?
items.e: Area = length × width: x(x + 7) = 24. Expand and make one side 0: x2 + 7x − 24 = 0.

items.q: A square lawn of side x m has a path 2 m wide all round it. The path has an area of 176 m². Which equation is correct?
items.e: (x + 4)2 − x2 = 176. The x2 terms cancel, leaving 8x − 160 = 0. Not every problem gives a quadratic.

items.q: The product of two consecutive whole numbers is 420. If the smaller number is x, which equation is correct?

items.q: The sum of the squares of two consecutive even numbers is 52. If both numbers are positive, what is the smaller one?
items.e: x2 + (x + 2)2 = 52 gives 2x2 + 4x − 48 = 0. Divide by 2: x2 + 2x − 24 = 0, so (x − 4)(x + 6) = 0. The answer is 4.

items.q: A ball is thrown upwards. Its height after t seconds is 30t − 5t2 metres. At what times is it 40 m above the ground?

items.q: A garden is 10 m by 17 m. A path of the same width goes all round it, and the path has an area of 41 m². Find the width of the path, correct to 2 decimal places.
A positive number x satisfies x(x + 9) = 23. Find x, correct to 2 decimal places.
Ethan cycles 18 km at x km/h. Cycling 4 km/h faster would save 2 hours. Find x, correct to 2 decimal places.
items.e: 18 ÷ x − 18 ÷ (x + 4) = 2 gives 2x2 + 8x − 72 = 0. The positive root is 4.32.

items.q: A rectangle is 3 cm longer than it is wide, and its area is 123 cm². Find its width, correct to 2 decimal places.
items.e: x2 + 3x − 123 = 0. x = (−3 ± √501) ÷ 2. The width is positive: 9.69 cm.
